cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Psoas major muscle

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Flexes the hip; with the femur fixed, flexes the trunk and laterally flexes the lumbar spine; stabilises the lumbar spine.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Anterior rami of L1–L3 (sometimes L4).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Sides of T12–L5 vertebral bodies and intervening discs; transverse processes of L1–L5.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Lesser trochanter of femur via the iliopsoas tendon.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Iliacus muscle

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Flexes the hip and stabilises the hip joint.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Femoral nerve (L2–L3).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Iliac fossa, inner lip of iliac crest, ala of sacrum and anterior sacroiliac ligaments.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Lesser trochanter and adjacent femur through and beside the iliopsoas tendon.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Gluteus maximus muscle

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Extends and laterally rotates the hip; especially active when rising or climbing; helps stabilise the knee through the iliotibial tract.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Inferior gluteal nerve (L5–S2).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Ilium posterior to the posterior gluteal line; dorsal sacrum and coccyx; sacrotuberous ligament.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Iliotibial tract and gluteal tuberosity of femur.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Gluteus medius muscle

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Abducts the hip; anterior fibres medially rotate it; holds the pelvis level during single-leg stance.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Superior gluteal nerve (L4–S1).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: External ilium between anterior and posterior gluteal lines.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Lateral surface of greater trochanter.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Piriformis muscle

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Laterally rotates the extended hip; abducts the flexed hip; stabilises the femoral head.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Nerve to piriformis (S1–S2).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Anterior sacrum, mainly between anterior sacral foramina; contributions from sacrotuberous ligament.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Superior border of greater trochanter.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Obturator internus

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Laterally rotates the extended hip; abducts the flexed hip; stabilises the femoral head.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Nerve to obturator internus (L5–S2).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Pelvic surface of obturator membrane and surrounding pubis and ischium.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Medial surface of greater trochanter, anterior to the trochanteric fossa, with the gemelli.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Gemellus superior muscle
cards.label: 7a

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Assists obturator internus in lateral rotation of the extended hip and abduction of the flexed hip.
cards.label: 7a

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Nerve to obturator internus (L5–S2).
cards.label: 7a

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Ischial spine.
cards.label: 7a

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Medial greater trochanter through the obturator internus tendon.
cards.label: 7a

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Gemellus inferior muscle
cards.label: 7b

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Assists obturator internus in lateral rotation of the extended hip and abduction of the flexed hip.
cards.label: 7b

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Nerve to quadratus femoris (L4–S1).
cards.label: 7b

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Upper part of ischial tuberosity.
cards.label: 7b

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Medial greater trochanter through the obturator internus tendon.
cards.label: 7b

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Quadratus femoris muscle

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Laterally rotates and assists adduction of the hip; stabilises the femoral head.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Nerve to quadratus femoris (L4–S1).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Lateral border of ischial tuberosity.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Quadrate tubercle on intertrochanteric crest and adjacent femur.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Tensor fasciae latae muscle

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Flexes, abducts and medially rotates the hip; tensions the iliotibial tract to stabilise the pelvis and knee.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Superior gluteal nerve (L4–S1).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: ASIS and anterior outer lip of iliac crest.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Iliotibial tract, which attaches to the lateral condyle of tibia at Gerdy’s tubercle.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Sartorius muscle

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Flexes, abducts and laterally rotates the hip; flexes the knee and medially rotates the leg when the knee is flexed.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Femoral nerve (L2–L3).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: ASIS and notch immediately inferior to it.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Superior medial tibia as part of the pes anserinus.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Quadriceps femoris muscle

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Extends the knee; rectus femoris also flexes the hip.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Femoral nerve (L2–L4).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Rectus femoris arises from the pelvis; the three vasti arise from the femur (see sublabels).

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Patella through the quadriceps tendon, then tibial tuberosity through the patellar ligament.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Rectus femoris
cards.label: 11a

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Extends the knee and flexes the hip.
cards.label: 11a

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Femoral nerve (L2–L4).
cards.label: 11a

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: AIIS (straight head) and ilium superior to acetabulum (reflected head).
cards.label: 11a

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Base of patella via quadriceps tendon; tibial tuberosity via patellar ligament.
cards.label: 11a

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Vastus medialis
cards.label: 11b

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Extends the knee; distal oblique fibres help resist lateral displacement of the patella.
cards.label: 11b

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Femoral nerve (L2–L4).
cards.label: 11b

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Lower intertrochanteric line, medial lip of linea aspera and medial supracondylar line.
cards.label: 11b

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Patella via quadriceps tendon and medial patellar retinaculum; tibial tuberosity via patellar ligament.
cards.label: 11b

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Vastus lateralis
cards.label: 11c

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Extends the knee.
cards.label: 11c

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Femoral nerve (L2–L4).
cards.label: 11c

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Greater trochanter, gluteal tuberosity and lateral lip of linea aspera.
cards.label: 11c

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Patella via quadriceps tendon and lateral patellar retinaculum; tibial tuberosity via patellar ligament.
cards.label: 11c

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Vastus intermedius
cards.label: 11d

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Extends the knee.
cards.label: 11d

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Femoral nerve (L2–L4).
cards.label: 11d

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Anterior and lateral surfaces of proximal two-thirds of femoral shaft.
cards.label: 11d

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Patella via quadriceps tendon; tibial tuberosity via patellar ligament.
cards.label: 11d

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Common tendon of quadriceps femoris
cards.label: 11e

cards.question: Formed by
cards.answer: Convergence of the tendons of rectus femoris and the three vasti.
cards.label: 11e

cards.question: Attachments
cards.answer: Quadriceps muscle proximally; base and margins of patella distally. Force continues to the tibial tuberosity through the patellar ligament.
cards.label: 11e

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Transmits quadriceps force to extend the knee.
cards.label: 11e

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Anterior to distal femur and knee joint; suprapatellar recess lies deep to it.
cards.label: 11e

cards.question: Clinical relevance
cards.answer: Complete rupture disrupts active knee extension and the straight-leg raise.
cards.label: 11e

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Pectineus muscle

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Adducts and flexes the hip; may assist medial rotation.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Usually femoral nerve (L2–L3); variable additional obturator or accessory obturator supply.

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Pecten pubis on superior pubic ramus.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Pectineal line of femur, inferior to lesser trochanter.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Adductor longus muscle

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Adducts the hip and assists hip flexion.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Anterior division of obturator nerve (L2–L4).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Body of pubis inferior to pubic crest.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Middle third of linea aspera.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Adductor magnus muscle

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Adductor part adducts and assists flexion of the hip; hamstring part extends the hip.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Adductor part: posterior division of obturator nerve (L2–L4). Hamstring part: tibial division of sciatic nerve, mainly L4.

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Adductor part: inferior pubic ramus and ramus of ischium. Hamstring part: ischial tuberosity.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Adductor part: gluteal tuberosity, linea aspera and medial supracondylar line. Hamstring part: adductor tubercle of femur.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Gracilis muscle

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Adducts the hip; flexes the knee and medially rotates the flexed leg.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Anterior division of obturator nerve (L2–L3).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Body and inferior ramus of pubis.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Superior medial tibia as part of pes anserinus.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Semitendinosus muscle

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Extends the hip; flexes the knee and medially rotates the flexed leg.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Tibial division of sciatic nerve (L5–S2).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Ischial tuberosity, sharing a proximal tendon with long head of biceps femoris.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Superior medial tibia as part of pes anserinus.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Semimembranosus muscle

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Extends the hip; flexes the knee and medially rotates the flexed leg.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Tibial division of sciatic nerve (L5–S2).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Superolateral impression of ischial tuberosity.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Posterior medial tibial condyle; expansion forms the oblique popliteal ligament.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Long head of biceps femoris muscle
cards.label: 18a

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Extends the hip; flexes the knee and laterally rotates the flexed leg.
cards.label: 18a

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Tibial division of sciatic nerve (L5–S2).
cards.label: 18a

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Ischial tuberosity, sharing a proximal tendon with semitendinosus.
cards.label: 18a

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Lateral aspect of head of fibula through the common biceps femoris tendon.
cards.label: 18a

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Short head of biceps femoris muscle
cards.label: 18b

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Flexes the knee and laterally rotates the flexed leg; does not cross the hip.
cards.label: 18b

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Common fibular division of sciatic nerve (L5–S2).
cards.label: 18b

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Lateral lip of linea aspera and lateral supracondylar line of femur.
cards.label: 18b

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Head of fibula through the common biceps femoris tendon.
cards.label: 18b

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Tibialis anterior muscle

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Dorsiflexes the ankle and inverts the foot; supports the medial longitudinal arch.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Deep fibular nerve (L4–L5).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Lateral tibial condyle, upper lateral tibial shaft and interosseous membrane.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Medial and plantar surfaces of medial cuneiform and base of first metatarsal.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Extensor hallucis longus muscle

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Extends the great toe at both joints; dorsiflexes the ankle.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Deep fibular nerve (L5–S1).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Middle anterior fibula and interosseous membrane.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Dorsal base of distal phalanx of great toe.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Extensor digitorum longus muscle

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Extends toes 2–5 at metatarsophalangeal and interphalangeal joints; dorsiflexes the ankle and assists eversion.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Deep fibular nerve (L5–S1).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Lateral tibial condyle, upper anterior fibula and interosseous membrane.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Extensor expansions of toes 2–5, reaching middle and distal phalanges.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Fibularis (or peroneus) longus muscle

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Everts the foot and weakly plantarflexes the ankle; supports transverse and longitudinal arches.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Superficial fibular nerve (L5–S2).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Head and upper two-thirds of lateral fibula.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Plantar surfaces of medial cuneiform and base of first metatarsal, after crossing the sole.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Fibularis (or peroneus) brevis muscle

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Everts the foot and weakly plantarflexes the ankle.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Superficial fibular nerve (L5–S2).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Lower two-thirds of lateral fibula.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Tuberosity at base of fifth metatarsal.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Triceps surae muscle group

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Plantarflexes the ankle and raises the heel; gastrocnemius also flexes the knee; soleus helps maintain standing posture.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Tibial nerve (mainly S1–S2).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Gastrocnemius: distal femur above both condyles. Soleus: posterior proximal tibia and fibula.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Posterior calcaneus through calcaneal tendon.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Medial head of gastrocnemius muscle
cards.label: 24a

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Plantarflexes the ankle and flexes the knee.
cards.label: 24a

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Tibial nerve (S1–S2).
cards.label: 24a

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Posterior femur superior to medial condyle and adjacent knee capsule.
cards.label: 24a

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Posterior calcaneus via calcaneal tendon.
cards.label: 24a

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Lateral head of gastrocnemius muscle
cards.label: 24b

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Plantarflexes the ankle and flexes the knee.
cards.label: 24b

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Tibial nerve (S1–S2).
cards.label: 24b

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Lateral aspect of lateral femoral condyle and adjacent knee capsule.
cards.label: 24b

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Posterior calcaneus via calcaneal tendon.
cards.label: 24b

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Soleus muscle
cards.label: 24c

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Plantarflexes the ankle; stabilises the leg on the foot during standing.
cards.label: 24c

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Tibial nerve (S1–S2).
cards.label: 24c

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Posterior head and proximal fibula, soleal line and medial tibial border, and tendinous arch between tibia and fibula.
cards.label: 24c

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Posterior calcaneus via calcaneal tendon.
cards.label: 24c

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Calcaneal (or Achilles) tendon
cards.label: 24d

cards.question: Formed by
cards.answer: Gastrocnemius and soleus tendons; plantaris usually runs separately alongside it.
cards.label: 24d

cards.question: Attachments
cards.answer: Triceps surae proximally; middle part of posterior calcaneal surface distally.
cards.label: 24d

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Transmits force for plantarflexion and push-off.
cards.label: 24d

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Superficial posterior ankle; retrocalcaneal bursa separates it from upper posterior calcaneus.
cards.label: 24d

cards.question: Clinical relevance
cards.answer: Rupture impairs push-off; squeezing the calf fails to produce normal plantarflexion (Thompson test). Ankle jerk mainly tests S1 through the tibial nerve.
cards.label: 24d

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Plantaris muscle

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Weakly assists knee flexion and ankle plantarflexion.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Tibial nerve (S1–S2).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Inferior lateral supracondylar line of femur and oblique popliteal ligament.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Posterior calcaneus, usually medial to calcaneal tendon; attachment varies.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Popliteus muscle

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Unlocks the extended knee by laterally rotating the femur on a fixed tibia, or medially rotating a free tibia; weakly flexes the knee.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Tibial nerve (L4–S1).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Lateral femoral condyle; tendon also connects to lateral meniscus.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Posterior tibia above soleal line.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Flexor digitorum longus muscle

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Flexes toes 2–5, especially distal interphalangeal joints; assists plantarflexion and supports longitudinal arches.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Tibial nerve (S2–S3).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Posterior tibia inferior to soleal line.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Plantar bases of distal phalanges of toes 2–5.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Tibialis posterior muscle

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Inverts the foot and assists plantarflexion; supports the medial longitudinal arch.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Tibial nerve (L4–L5).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Posterior tibia and fibula and intervening interosseous membrane.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Mainly navicular tuberosity, with expansions to cuneiforms, cuboid, sustentaculum tali and bases of metatarsals 2–4.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Flexor hallucis longus muscle

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Flexes the great toe, especially its interphalangeal joint; assists plantarflexion and push-off; supports medial longitudinal arch.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Tibial nerve (S2–S3).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Inferior two-thirds of posterior fibula and adjacent interosseous membrane.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Plantar base of distal phalanx of great toe.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Extensor hallucis brevis muscle

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Extends the great toe at the metatarsophalangeal joint.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Deep fibular nerve (L5–S1).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Superolateral calcaneus, continuous with extensor digitorum brevis.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Dorsal base of proximal phalanx of great toe.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Extensor digitorum brevis muscle

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Assists extension of toes 2–4 at metatarsophalangeal and interphalangeal joints.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Deep fibular nerve (L5–S1).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Superolateral calcaneus and inferior extensor retinaculum.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Extensor digitorum longus tendons/extensor expansions of toes 2–4.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Abductor hallucis muscle

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Abducts the great toe and assists its metatarsophalangeal flexion; supports medial longitudinal arch.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Medial plantar nerve (S2–S3).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Medial process of calcaneal tuberosity, flexor retinaculum and plantar aponeurosis.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Medial base of proximal phalanx of great toe, with medial sesamoid and medial flexor hallucis brevis tendon.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Medial head of flexor hallucis brevis (lateral head is not labelled)

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Flexes the great toe at its metatarsophalangeal joint; supports the medial forefoot.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Medial plantar nerve (S2–S3).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Shared proximal origin from plantar cuboid and lateral cuneiform, with a contribution from tibialis posterior tendon.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Medial base of proximal phalanx of great toe through a tendon containing the medial sesamoid.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Abductor digiti minimi muscle

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Abducts and assists flexion of the fifth toe at its metatarsophalangeal joint; supports lateral longitudinal arch.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Lateral plantar nerve (S2–S3).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Medial and lateral processes of calcaneal tuberosity and plantar aponeurosis.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Lateral base of proximal phalanx of fifth toe; often an additional slip to fifth metatarsal base.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Flexor digiti minimi muscle

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Flexes the fifth toe at its metatarsophalangeal joint (the foot muscle is also called flexor digiti minimi brevis).

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Superficial branch of lateral plantar nerve (S2–S3).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Plantar base of fifth metatarsal and sheath of fibularis longus tendon.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Base of proximal phalanx of fifth toe.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Flexor digitorum brevis

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Flexes toes 2–5 at proximal interphalangeal joints and assists metatarsophalangeal flexion; supports longitudinal arches.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Medial plantar nerve (S2–S3).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Medial process of calcaneal tuberosity and plantar aponeurosis.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Both sides of middle phalanges of toes 2–5; each tendon splits around a flexor digitorum longus tendon.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Lumbrical muscles

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Flex metatarsophalangeal joints and extend interphalangeal joints of toes 2–5.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: First: medial plantar nerve. Second–fourth: deep branch of lateral plantar nerve (S2–S3).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Tendons of flexor digitorum longus; first is unipennate, others bipennate.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Medial sides of extensor expansions of toes 2–5.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Dorsal interosseus muscles

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Abduct toes 2–4 relative to the second toe; assist metatarsophalangeal flexion and interphalangeal extension.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Deep branch of lateral plantar nerve (S2–S3).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Adjacent sides of metatarsals 1–5; four bipennate muscles.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: First: medial base of second proximal phalanx. Others: lateral bases of proximal phalanges of toes 2–4; also extensor expansions.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Common iliac artery

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Abdominal aortic bifurcation, usually at L4.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Runs inferolaterally along medial psoas border; divides near the sacroiliac joint.

cards.question: Branches
cards.answer: Internal and external iliac arteries.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Pelvis and lower limb through its terminal branches.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Common iliac veins lie posterior; the ureter crosses the iliac vessels near their bifurcation.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: External iliac vein
cards.label: 39a

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Continuation of femoral vein proximal to inguinal ligament.
cards.label: 39a

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Ascends along pelvic brim, initially medial to external iliac artery.
cards.label: 39a

cards.question: Tributaries
cards.answer: Inferior epigastric and deep circumflex iliac veins; pubic tributaries may occur.
cards.label: 39a

cards.question: Drainage
cards.answer: Most venous blood from lower limb and part of lower anterior abdominal wall.
cards.label: 39a

cards.question: Terminates as
cards.answer: Joins internal iliac vein to form common iliac vein near sacroiliac joint.
cards.label: 39a

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Internal iliac artery

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Common iliac artery near sacroiliac joint.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Descends into lesser pelvis; usually divides into anterior and posterior divisions.

cards.question: Branches
cards.answer: Posterior division: iliolumbar, lateral sacral, superior gluteal. Anterior division commonly gives obturator, inferior gluteal, internal pudendal, umbilical/superior vesical, middle rectal and sex-dependent visceral branches.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Pelvic walls and viscera, gluteal region, perineum and part of medial thigh.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Branching is variable; lies anterior to the internal iliac vein.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Obturator artery

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Usually anterior division of internal iliac artery; may arise from inferior epigastric/external iliac system.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Follows lateral pelvic wall into obturator canal, then divides around obturator foramen.

cards.question: Branches
cards.answer: Anterior and posterior branches; pubic and acetabular branches.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Medial thigh, obturator muscles and part of hip joint; acetabular branch contributes variably to femoral head.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Obturator nerve, artery and vein pass through obturator canal; pubic vascular connections can form a corona mortis over superior pubic ramus.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Superior gluteal artery

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Posterior division of internal iliac artery.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Leaves pelvis through greater sciatic foramen above piriformis; divides in gluteal region.

cards.question: Branches
cards.answer: Superficial and deep branches.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Gluteus medius, minimus, part of maximus, tensor fasciae latae and hip region.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Travels with superior gluteal nerve; deep branch runs between gluteus medius and minimus.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Inferior gluteal artery

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Usually anterior division of internal iliac artery.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Leaves greater sciatic foramen below piriformis and descends deep to gluteus maximus.

cards.question: Branches
cards.answer: Muscular and anastomotic branches; artery accompanying sciatic nerve.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Gluteus maximus, short lateral rotators, proximal hamstrings and sciatic nerve.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Accompanies inferior gluteal nerve; contributes to cruciate anastomosis.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Internal pudendal artery

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Anterior division of internal iliac artery.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Exits greater sciatic foramen below piriformis, hooks around ischial spine, enters lesser sciatic foramen and runs in pudendal canal.

cards.question: Branches
cards.answer: Inferior rectal, perineal, urethral and genital branches, including deep and dorsal arteries of penis or clitoris.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Perineum, external genitalia and lower anal canal.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Travels with pudendal nerve near sacrospinous ligament and then in obturator fascia along lateral wall of ischioanal fossa.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Femoral artery

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Continuation of external iliac artery distal to inguinal ligament.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Passes through femoral triangle and adductor canal; becomes popliteal artery at adductor hiatus.

cards.question: Branches
cards.answer: Superficial epigastric, superficial circumflex iliac, external pudendal, profunda femoris, muscular and descending genicular branches.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Main arterial inflow to lower limb; directly supplies anterior thigh and superficial groin regions.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: At inguinal ligament, nerve is lateral and vein medial to artery; nerve lies outside femoral sheath. Pulse is at mid-inguinal point, halfway between ASIS and pubic symphysis.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Profunda femoris artery (deep artery of the thigh)

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Usually posterolateral femoral artery a few centimetres below inguinal ligament.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Passes deep to adductor longus, descending close to femur between adductor muscles.

cards.question: Branches
cards.answer: Medial and lateral circumflex femoral arteries; usually three perforating branches, with terminal continuation often counted as fourth.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Major deep supply to thigh muscles and femur.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Lies posterior to adductor longus; perforating branches pierce adductor magnus.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Lateral circumflex femoral artery

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Usually profunda femoris; sometimes femoral artery.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Runs laterally deep to sartorius and rectus femoris, between femoral nerve divisions.

cards.question: Branches
cards.answer: Ascending, transverse and descending branches.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Anterior/lateral thigh, hip region and knee through descending branch.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Ascending branch of lateral circumflex femoral artery

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Lateral circumflex femoral artery.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Ascends toward greater trochanter, deep to tensor fasciae latae.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Lateral hip muscles and hip region; contributes to trochanteric anastomosis.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Medial circumflex femoral artery

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Usually profunda femoris; may arise directly from femoral artery.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Passes medially and posteriorly between pectineus and iliopsoas, then around proximal femur.

cards.question: Branches
cards.answer: Deep and superficial branches; ascending/retinacular and transverse branches.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Principal adult supply to femoral head and neck through retinacular branches; also medial thigh muscles.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Retinacular vessels ascend along femoral neck beneath capsule and may be torn by an intracapsular femoral neck fracture.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Perforating artery from profunda femoris artery

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Profunda femoris artery.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Pierces adductor magnus near linea aspera to reach posterior thigh.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Hamstrings, adductors, vastus lateralis and femur; joins longitudinal anastomoses along posterior thigh.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Popliteal artery

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Continuation of femoral artery at adductor hiatus.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Descends through popliteal fossa; at lower border of popliteus gives anterior tibial artery and a short tibioperoneal trunk leading to posterior tibial and fibular arteries.

cards.question: Branches
cards.answer: Five genicular arteries, sural/muscular branches, anterior tibial artery and tibioperoneal trunk.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Knee joint and surrounding muscles; distal limb through terminal branches.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Deepest central structure in popliteal fossa: nerve, vein, artery from superficial to deep; lies against femur, posterior knee capsule and popliteus.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Superior lateral geniculate artery

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Popliteal artery above knee joint.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Winds around lateral femoral condyle deep to biceps femoris tendon.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Superolateral knee and genicular anastomosis; also adjacent vastus lateralis.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Superior medial geniculate artery

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Popliteal artery above knee joint.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Passes around medial femoral condyle deep to adductor magnus tendon.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Superomedial knee and genicular anastomosis; also adjacent vastus medialis.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Inferior lateral geniculate artery

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Popliteal artery near knee joint level.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Passes laterally over popliteus, deep to fibular collateral ligament, toward front of knee.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Inferolateral knee and genicular anastomosis.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Inferior medial geniculate artery

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Popliteal artery near knee joint level.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Passes below medial tibial condyle, deep to tibial collateral ligament.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Inferomedial knee and genicular anastomosis.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Posterior tibial artery

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Terminal branch of tibioperoneal trunk from popliteal artery; often described as a terminal popliteal branch.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Descends in deep posterior leg; passes behind medial malleolus beneath flexor retinaculum; divides into medial and lateral plantar arteries.

cards.question: Branches
cards.answer: Muscular, nutrient tibial, medial malleolar and calcaneal branches; medial and lateral plantar terminal branches. Fibular artery is often described as its proximal branch.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Posterior leg and plantar foot.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: At medial ankle lies between flexor digitorum longus tendon and tibial nerve; pulse is palpable posterior to medial malleolus.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Anterior tibial artery

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Popliteal artery at lower border of popliteus.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Passes through proximal interosseous membrane into anterior compartment; descends on membrane and continues as dorsalis pedis at ankle.

cards.question: Branches
cards.answer: Anterior tibial recurrent, muscular and anterior medial/lateral malleolar branches.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Anterior leg and, through dorsalis pedis, dorsum of foot.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Travels with deep fibular nerve; distally lies between tibialis anterior and extensor hallucis longus, then between extensor hallucis longus and extensor digitorum longus tendons.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Fibular (or peroneal) artery

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Tibioperoneal trunk; commonly described as a proximal branch of posterior tibial artery.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Descends close to medial side of fibula in deep posterior compartment, deep to flexor hallucis longus.

cards.question: Branches
cards.answer: Muscular, nutrient fibular, perforating, communicating and calcaneal branches.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Lateral and deep posterior leg, fibula, and lateral ankle/heel.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Femoral nerve

cards.question: Roots
cards.answer: L2–L4, posterior divisions of anterior rami.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Emerges lateral to psoas major; runs between psoas and iliacus, beneath inguinal ligament and lateral to femoral artery; divides in femoral triangle.

cards.question: Motor functions
cards.answer: Knee extension through quadriceps; hip flexion through iliacus and sartorius; usually supplies pectineus.

cards.question: Sensory functions
cards.answer: Anterior thigh through anterior cutaneous branches; medial leg and medial foot through saphenous nerve; articular branches to hip and knee.

cards.question: Lesion
cards.answer: Proximal lesion causes weak knee extension, reduced/absent patellar reflex (L3–L4, chiefly L4), and sensory loss over anterior thigh and medial leg; hip flexion is weakened but psoas is spared.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Saphenous nerve

cards.question: Roots
cards.answer: L3–L4; sensory branch of femoral nerve.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Travels in adductor canal with femoral vessels; leaves before adductor hiatus, emerges medially around knee and descends with great saphenous vein.

cards.question: Motor functions
cards.answer: None; purely sensory.

cards.question: Sensory functions
cards.answer: Medial knee, medial leg and medial border of foot, with variable distal extent.

cards.question: Lesion
cards.answer: Numbness or neuropathic pain in medial leg/foot without motor weakness; vulnerable during medial knee procedures and great saphenous vein harvesting.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Obturator nerve

cards.question: Roots
cards.answer: L2–L4, anterior divisions of anterior rami.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Emerges medial to psoas; follows lateral pelvic wall through obturator canal; anterior and posterior divisions pass on either side of adductor brevis.

cards.question: Motor functions
cards.answer: Hip adduction through adductor longus, brevis, adductor part of magnus and gracilis; supplies obturator externus; variable contribution to pectineus.

cards.question: Sensory functions
cards.answer: Small, variable medial thigh skin territory; articular branches to hip and knee.

cards.question: Lesion
cards.answer: Weak thigh adduction, sometimes medial thigh sensory loss or pain; hip pathology may cause referred knee pain through articular branches.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Sacral plexus

cards.question: Roots
cards.answer: L4–S4 anterior rami; L4–L5 arrive via lumbosacral trunk.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Lies on anterior surface of piriformis on posterior pelvic wall; many branches leave via greater sciatic foramen.

cards.question: Motor functions
cards.answer: Via branches: gluteal muscles, short hip rotators, hamstrings, most of adductor magnus hamstring part, all leg and foot muscles, and perineal muscles.

cards.question: Sensory functions
cards.answer: Via branches: posterior thigh, most of leg and foot, and perineum; excludes femoral/saphenous and obturator territories.

cards.question: Lesion
cards.answer: Deficits span several nerves: variable hip, knee, ankle and foot weakness with broad sensory loss; lower plexus involvement may affect perineal sensation and sphincter control.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Sciatic nerve

cards.question: Roots
cards.answer: L4–S3; tibial component from anterior divisions and common fibular component from posterior divisions.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Usually leaves greater sciatic foramen below piriformis; passes deep to gluteus maximus between greater trochanter and ischial tuberosity, then down posterior thigh; usually divides near upper popliteal fossa, but division level varies.

cards.question: Motor functions
cards.answer: Hamstrings and hamstring part of adductor magnus; through terminal branches, all leg and foot muscles.

cards.question: Sensory functions
cards.answer: No direct cutaneous branches in thigh; terminal branches supply most leg and foot except saphenous territory.

cards.question: Lesion
cards.answer: High lesion weakens knee flexion and severely impairs ankle/toe movement, often causing foot drop; sensory loss affects much of leg/foot while medial leg is spared. Posterior thigh skin is mainly supplied by a separate nerve.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Tibial nerve

cards.question: Roots
cards.answer: L4–S3; anterior divisions through sciatic nerve.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Runs centrally through popliteal fossa, beneath soleal arch and down deep posterior leg; passes behind medial malleolus through tarsal tunnel and divides into medial/lateral plantar nerves.

cards.question: Motor functions
cards.answer: Plantarflexion, toe flexion and inversion through posterior leg muscles; most intrinsic foot actions through plantar branches; popliteus unlocks knee.

cards.question: Sensory functions
cards.answer: Heel through calcaneal branches, sole through plantar nerves; contributes to sural nerve supplying posterolateral distal leg and lateral foot.

cards.question: Lesion
cards.answer: Proximal lesion causes weak plantarflexion, inversion and toe flexion, inability to stand normally on tiptoe, sole sensory loss and reduced Achilles reflex (mainly S1). Distal tarsal tunnel lesions mainly affect plantar sensation and intrinsic foot muscles.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Common fibular (peroneal) nerve

cards.question: Roots
cards.answer: L4–S2; posterior divisions through sciatic nerve.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Follows medial border of biceps femoris tendon along lateral popliteal fossa; winds around fibular neck and divides into superficial and deep fibular nerves.

cards.question: Motor functions
cards.answer: Through branches: dorsiflexion, toe extension and eversion. Its sciatic component supplies short head of biceps femoris before the usual terminal division.

cards.question: Sensory functions
cards.answer: Upper lateral leg through lateral sural cutaneous branch; terminal branches supply anterolateral distal leg and most dorsal foot; contributes variably to sural nerve.

cards.question: Lesion
cards.answer: Fibular neck injury causes foot drop, weak eversion and dorsal foot sensory loss; inversion is relatively preserved through tibialis posterior, helping distinguish it from an L5 root lesion.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Deep fibular (peroneal) nerve

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Enters anterior compartment, accompanies anterior tibial vessels and passes beneath extensor retinacula onto dorsum of foot.

cards.question: Motor functions
cards.answer: Dorsiflexion and toe extension through anterior leg muscles; supplies extensor digitorum brevis and extensor hallucis brevis.

cards.question: Sensory functions
cards.answer: First dorsal web space between great and second toes; also joint branches.

cards.question: Lesion
cards.answer: Proximal lesion causes foot drop and weak toe extension with first web-space sensory loss; distal entrapment at ankle may spare leg muscles.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Superficial fibular (peroneal) nerve

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Descends in lateral leg compartment, supplies fibularis longus/brevis, pierces deep fascia in distal leg and divides across dorsal foot.

cards.question: Motor functions
cards.answer: Foot eversion through fibularis longus and brevis; assists weak plantarflexion.

cards.question: Sensory functions
cards.answer: Anterolateral distal leg and most dorsum of foot, excluding first web space and usually lateral border; toe tips/nail beds are mainly plantar nerve territory.

cards.question: Lesion
cards.answer: Weak eversion and altered dorsal foot sensation, with dorsiflexion and first web-space sensation preserved in an isolated lesion.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Fifth lumbar vertebra

cards.question: Articulations
cards.answer: L4 superiorly and sacrum inferiorly through intervertebral discs and paired facet joints.

cards.question: Landmarks
cards.answer: Large body, pedicles, laminae, short broad spinous process, transverse processes and superior/inferior articular processes.

cards.question: Muscle attachments
cards.answer: Psoas major attaches to body/transverse process; multifidus to spinous process and mammillary region; intertransversarii and other deep back muscles attach to posterior elements.

cards.question: Orientation
cards.answer: Body faces anteriorly; spinous process posteriorly; superior facets face mainly medially. L5 has a large body adapted to the lumbosacral junction; it is a midline bone.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Sacrum

cards.question: Articulations
cards.answer: L5 at lumbosacral joint, both ilia at sacroiliac joints, and coccyx at sacrococcygeal joint.

cards.question: Landmarks
cards.answer: Promontory, alae, anterior/posterior sacral foramina, median sacral crest, auricular surfaces, sacral canal, hiatus and cornua.

cards.question: Muscle attachments
cards.answer: Piriformis on pelvic surface; gluteus maximus and multifidus posteriorly; iliacus may arise from ala; pelvic floor muscles attach near lower lateral sacrum.

cards.question: Orientation
cards.answer: Broad base superior, apex inferior; smooth concave surface anterior; rough crested surface posterior. Auricular surfaces face laterally.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Coccyx

cards.question: Articulations
cards.answer: Sacrum superiorly; small joints between coccygeal segments may fuse.

cards.question: Landmarks
cards.answer: Usually 3–5 fused or partly fused vertebral segments; base, apex, coccygeal cornua and first-segment transverse processes.

cards.question: Muscle attachments
cards.answer: Coccygeus and levator ani attach to sides/anterior aspect; gluteus maximus attaches posteriorly; anococcygeal body connects it to anal region.

cards.question: Orientation
cards.answer: Base superior toward sacrum; tapering apex inferior, usually curving anteriorly; cornua project upward from posterior base.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Iliac crest

cards.question: Bone
cards.answer: Ilium of hip bone.

cards.question: Attachments
cards.answer: External oblique to outer lip; internal oblique to intermediate zone; transversus abdominis to inner lip; tensor fasciae latae anteriorly; quadratus lumborum, erector spinae and thoracolumbar fascia posteriorly.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Superior rim between ASIS and PSIS; iliac tubercle lies on outer lip posterior to ASIS.

cards.question: Clinical relevance
cards.answer: Line between highest points of crests approximates L4 spinous process/L4–L5 interval; common landmark for lumbar procedures and bone graft harvesting.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Anterior superior iliac spine (ASIS)

cards.question: Bone
cards.answer: Ilium of hip bone.

cards.question: Attachments
cards.answer: Sartorius and inguinal ligament; tensor fasciae latae arises from ASIS and adjacent anterior crest.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Anterior end of iliac crest; lateral femoral cutaneous nerve usually passes near it beneath inguinal ligament.

cards.question: Clinical relevance
cards.answer: Landmark for measuring true anatomical limb length from ASIS to medial malleolus; nearby nerve compression causes meralgia paraesthetica.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Pubis bone

cards.question: Articulations
cards.answer: Meets opposite pubis at pubic symphysis; fuses with ilium and ischium in hip bone and contributes to acetabulum articulating with femoral head.

cards.question: Landmarks
cards.answer: Body, superior and inferior rami, pubic crest, pubic tubercle, pecten pubis and obturator groove.

cards.question: Muscle attachments
cards.answer: Pectineus on superior ramus; adductor longus on body; adductor brevis, gracilis and adductor magnus on body/inferior ramus; rectus abdominis on crest/symphysis; obturator muscles around obturator foramen.

cards.question: Orientation
cards.answer: Symphyseal surface faces medially; body is anterior; acetabular contribution faces laterally; superior ramus lies above obturator foramen.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Pubic symphysis

cards.question: Joint type
cards.answer: Secondary cartilaginous joint (symphysis) with fibrocartilaginous interpubic disc between hyaline-covered pubic surfaces.

cards.question: Articulating bones
cards.answer: Right and left pubic bodies.

cards.question: Attachments
cards.answer: Superior and inferior (arcuate) pubic ligaments reinforce it; rectus abdominis and adductor longus aponeurotic fibres contribute anteriorly.

cards.question: Movement
cards.answer: Small amounts of translation and rotation; stabilises anterior pelvic ring while allowing limited compliance.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Anterior midline pelvis; bladder lies posterior, separated by retropubic space.

cards.question: Clinical relevance
cards.answer: May separate in pelvic injury or around childbirth; osteitis pubis causes pain around the joint.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Ischial spine

cards.question: Bone
cards.answer: Ischium of hip bone.

cards.question: Attachments
cards.answer: Sacrospinous ligament; superior gemellus; coccygeus; posterior attachment of tendinous arch of levator ani.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Separates greater and lesser sciatic notches; pudendal nerve and internal pudendal vessels pass near its posterior aspect.

cards.question: Clinical relevance
cards.answer: Palpable landmark for pudendal nerve block.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Ischial tuberosity

cards.question: Bone
cards.answer: Ischium of hip bone.

cards.question: Attachments
cards.answer: Semimembranosus, semitendinosus and long head of biceps femoris; hamstring part of adductor magnus; quadratus femoris, inferior gemellus and sacrotuberous ligament.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Supports body weight in sitting; sciatic nerve runs lateral to it, deep to gluteus maximus.

cards.question: Clinical relevance
cards.answer: Site of proximal hamstring avulsion and ischial bursitis.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Greater trochanter

cards.question: Bone
cards.answer: Proximal femur.

cards.question: Attachments
cards.answer: Gluteus medius laterally, minimus anteriorly, piriformis superiorly, obturator internus/gemelli medially; obturator externus inserts into trochanteric fossa. Vastus lateralis arises partly from it.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Large lateral projection beside femoral neck; covered by gluteal tendons and bursae beneath iliotibial tract.

cards.question: Clinical relevance
cards.answer: Lateral hip pain may arise from gluteal tendinopathy and associated trochanteric bursae.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Lesser trochanter

cards.question: Bone
cards.answer: Proximal femur.

cards.question: Attachments
cards.answer: Iliopsoas tendon insertion.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Posteromedial projection at neck–shaft junction; pectineal line descends from its vicinity.

cards.question: Clinical relevance
cards.answer: May be avulsed by forceful iliopsoas contraction in adolescents.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Femur

cards.question: Articulations
cards.answer: Acetabulum at hip; tibia and patella at knee.

cards.question: Landmarks
cards.answer: Head and fovea, neck, greater/lesser trochanters, intertrochanteric line/crest, gluteal tuberosity, linea aspera, condyles, epicondyles, adductor tubercle and intercondylar fossa.

cards.question: Muscle attachments
cards.answer: Trochanters receive gluteal/short rotator/iliopsoas attachments; linea aspera receives adductors and origins of vasti/short biceps head; gastrocnemius and popliteus arise distally.

cards.question: Orientation
cards.answer: Head points medially and slightly anteriorly; linea aspera and intercondylar fossa face posteriorly; patellar surface faces anteriorly. Position head toward the body midline to determine side.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Medial epicondyle of the femur

cards.question: Bone
cards.answer: Distal femur.

cards.question: Attachments
cards.answer: Femoral attachment of tibial (medial) collateral ligament; adductor magnus hamstring tendon attaches to nearby adductor tubercle superiorly.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Medial non-articular prominence above medial condyle; distinguish epicondyle from adductor tubercle.

cards.question: Clinical relevance
cards.answer: Medial collateral ligament injury follows valgus stress and may produce local tenderness.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Lateral epicondyle of the femur

cards.question: Bone
cards.answer: Distal femur.

cards.question: Attachments
cards.answer: Femoral attachment of fibular (lateral) collateral ligament.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Lateral non-articular prominence; popliteus tendon arises in adjacent groove on lateral condyle, below/anterior to collateral attachment.

cards.question: Clinical relevance
cards.answer: Fibular collateral ligament resists varus stress; injury can cause lateral knee instability.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Patella

cards.question: Articulations
cards.answer: Posterior surface articulates with femoral trochlea; no direct tibial articulation.

cards.question: Landmarks
cards.answer: Superior base, inferior apex, anterior surface and posterior medial/lateral articular facets separated by vertical ridge.

cards.question: Muscle attachments
cards.answer: Quadriceps tendon attaches to base and margins; force is transmitted from apex to tibial tuberosity by patellar ligament; patellar retinacula attach at sides.

cards.question: Orientation
cards.answer: Apex inferior; rough surface anterior; smooth facets posterior. Larger articular facet is lateral, helping determine side.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Tibia

cards.question: Articulations
cards.answer: Femur superiorly; fibula at proximal tibiofibular joint and distal syndesmosis; talus inferiorly.

cards.question: Landmarks
cards.answer: Medial/lateral condyles, intercondylar eminence, tibial tuberosity, anterior crest, soleal line, fibular notch and medial malleolus.

cards.question: Muscle attachments
cards.answer: Patellar ligament on tuberosity; pes anserinus on superior medial surface; semimembranosus posterior to medial condyle; popliteus above soleal line; soleus, tibialis anterior/posterior and flexor digitorum longus on shaft regions.

cards.question: Orientation
cards.answer: Broad condyles superior; tuberosity and sharp crest anterior; medial malleolus projects medially; distal fibular notch faces laterally.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Medial malleolus (of tibia)

cards.question: Bone
cards.answer: Distal tibia.

cards.question: Attachments
cards.answer: Deltoid ligament; flexor retinaculum along posterior region.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Forms medial ankle mortise and articulates with talus. Behind it run tibialis posterior, flexor digitorum longus, posterior tibial vessels, tibial nerve and flexor hallucis longus, from anterior to posterior.

cards.question: Clinical relevance
cards.answer: Fracture may accompany ankle instability; posterior tibial pulse lies behind it and tibial nerve can be compressed in tarsal tunnel.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Head of fibula

cards.question: Bone
cards.answer: Proximal fibula.

cards.question: Attachments
cards.answer: Biceps femoris tendon and fibular collateral ligament; soleus and fibularis longus arise partly from head.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Articulates with lateral tibial condyle; common fibular nerve winds around neck immediately distal to head.

cards.question: Clinical relevance
cards.answer: Proximal fibular injury can damage common fibular nerve and produce foot drop.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Fibula

cards.question: Articulations
cards.answer: Tibia at proximal tibiofibular joint and distal syndesmosis; talus at lateral malleolar facet. Does not articulate with femur.

cards.question: Landmarks
cards.answer: Head, apex, neck, shaft, interosseous border, lateral malleolus and malleolar fossa.

cards.question: Muscle attachments
cards.answer: Biceps femoris inserts on head; fibularis longus/brevis arise laterally; soleus, tibialis posterior and flexor hallucis longus posteriorly; toe extensors arise anteriorly.

cards.question: Orientation
cards.answer: Head superior; lateral malleolus inferior; malleolar articular facet faces medially and malleolar fossa posteriorly. Distal malleolus extends lower than tibial malleolus.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Lateral malleolus (of fibula)

cards.question: Bone
cards.answer: Distal fibula.

cards.question: Attachments
cards.answer: Anterior talofibular, posterior talofibular and calcaneofibular ligaments; superior fibular retinaculum posteriorly.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Forms lateral ankle mortise; fibularis brevis and longus tendons pass behind it, brevis usually anterior to longus.

cards.question: Clinical relevance
cards.answer: Common ankle fracture site; lateral ligament injury frequently accompanies inversion sprains.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Calcaneus

cards.question: Articulations
cards.answer: Talus superiorly at talocalcaneal facets; cuboid anteriorly.

cards.question: Landmarks
cards.answer: Calcaneal tuberosity, sustentaculum tali, talar facets, calcaneal sulcus and fibular trochlea.

cards.question: Muscle attachments
cards.answer: Calcaneal tendon posteriorly; plantar intrinsic muscles arise from tuberosity; quadratus plantae from plantar surface; extensor digitorum/hallucis brevis from superolateral surface.

cards.question: Orientation
cards.answer: Large tuberosity posterior, cuboid facet anterior, talar facets superior; sustentaculum tali projects medially. Flexor hallucis longus groove lies beneath sustentaculum.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Navicular

cards.question: Articulations
cards.answer: Talar head proximally; three cuneiforms distally; sometimes a facet for cuboid laterally.

cards.question: Landmarks
cards.answer: Medial navicular tuberosity, concave proximal talar facet and three distal cuneiform facets.

cards.question: Muscle attachments
cards.answer: Tibialis posterior has its principal insertion on navicular tuberosity.

cards.question: Orientation
cards.answer: Concave surface faces posteriorly toward talar head; divided distal surface anteriorly; tuberosity projects medially and plantarly.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: First metatarsal

cards.question: Articulations
cards.answer: Medial cuneiform proximally; great-toe proximal phalanx distally; two plantar sesamoids under head. Sometimes articulates with second metatarsal base.

cards.question: Landmarks
cards.answer: Base, short thick shaft, head and plantar sesamoid grooves.

cards.question: Muscle attachments
cards.answer: Tibialis anterior attaches medially at base; fibularis longus attaches plantarly at base; first dorsal interosseous arises from lateral side of shaft.

cards.question: Orientation
cards.answer: Base proximal, rounded head distal; sesamoid grooves plantar; bone lies at medial border of forefoot, with interosseous attachment toward second metatarsal.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Fifth metatarsal

cards.question: Articulations
cards.answer: Cuboid and fourth metatarsal proximally; proximal phalanx of fifth toe distally.

cards.question: Landmarks
cards.answer: Base, prominent lateral tuberosity, shaft and head.

cards.question: Muscle attachments
cards.answer: Fibularis brevis inserts at tuberosity; fibularis tertius on dorsal base; flexor digiti minimi brevis arises plantarly; interossei attach along shaft.

cards.question: Orientation
cards.answer: Tuberosity projects laterally from proximal base; rounded head distal; facet for fourth metatarsal faces medially.
